description:
Spatial convergence of the FLUX-FORM first-order-upwind vertical advection operator grids/latlon3d/rules/upwind1_flux_D_lev_noflux_bc, driven by problems/latlon3d_advection_vertical_upwind_flux. 

FORCED-STEADY (TRUNCATION) IDIOM, matching the sibling latlon3d_advection_vertical_ppm: u*(z) = cos(pi z) is an exact steady state of the forced equation, so the drift measured at t = 0.1 IS the operator's truncation error and the observed rate is the truncation order. Donor-cell upwinding is first order, hence expected_order 1.0. (Contrast the diffusion cases on this grid, which use the solution-error idiom at t = 0.1 because their boundary cells carry O(dz) truncation while Gustafsson's theorem keeps the solution error at O(dz^2). The idiom is chosen by operator type: parabolic -> solution error, hyperbolic flux-form -> truncation.)

THE LADDER STARTS AT 32, NOT 16, AND THIS IS DELIBERATE. The face velocity sin(2 pi z) carries a full wavelength across the domain, so a 16-cell mesh barely resolves the WIND, let alone the tracer, and the coarse rungs sit well outside the asymptotic regime: on a 16/32/64/128 ladder the Linf pairwise orders run 0.34, 0.78, 0.91, whose median (0.78) misses first order by 0.22 and would need an implausibly loose gate to pass. On 32/64/128/256 the same operator marches cleanly: L2 pairwise 0.94, 0.96, 0.97 (median 0.96) and Linf 0.78, 0.91, 0.99 (median 0.91). The fix is to measure in the asymptotic regime, NOT to slacken order_tolerance -- a loose tolerance on a pre-asymptotic ladder is exactly how a genuinely inconsistent scheme slips through. The sweep is cheap (~30 s for all four rungs) because advection is CFL-limited rather than dz^2-stiffness-limited, so the extra rung costs little. 

WHAT THIS GUARDS. The velocity is a declared THREE-DIMENSIONAL face-staggered field W[lon, lat, lev_nodes] that REVERSES SIGN at z = 1/2, so both branches of the donor-cell selection are exercised in every column, and the horizontal modulation a(i) b(j) means a stencil that mis-indexed W as a column profile would be caught rather than silently agreeing. No pre-existing advection operator on this grid can represent either property: they match a bare D(q, wrt: axis) with the velocity supplied from outside, and they hard-code a single flow direction.
